text: Diligence and focused effort are like the sprout that exists potentially within a seed; in the same way, through focused effort, one determines, "This shall be a pot" or "This shall be a cloth." That which is perceived as the intellect is the eight-fold, sattvic intellect. Due to the absence of formal difference, the sattvic form of the intellect is fourfold: Dharma (righteousness), Jnana (knowledge), Vairagya (detachment), and Aishvarya (divine power). Dharma is characterized by compassion, charity, Yama (restraints), and Niyama (observances). The Yamas and Niyamas are those stated by Patanjali. The Yamas are non-violence, truthfulness, non-stealing, continence, and non-possessiveness. The Niyamas are purity, contentment, austerity, self-study, and surrender to the Divine.
